home.heroTitle: Learn the market before you risk anything in it
home.heroBody: Plain-language lessons in the order they make sense: what a currency pair actually is, how to read what a chart is telling you, and how to size a position before you ever open one.
home.glossaryLead: Plain-language definitions for the terms you will meet on every chart.
home.newsletterBody: Analysis and education, delivered as it publishes.
home.faqLead: The things new traders ask us most often.
home.faqA1: Yes. Every lesson, glossary entry and market article on this site is free to read.
home.faqQ2: Do I need trading experience to start?
home.faqA2: No. The material starts from first principles and builds up, so a complete beginner can follow it.
home.faqA3: No. Everything here is educational. Nothing on this site is a recommendation to buy or sell any instrument.
home.faqQ4: How often is new analysis published?
home.faqA4: New articles and analysis are published regularly; the latest always appear on this page and in the News section.
home.exploreTitle: Everything a trader needs, in one place
home.exploreLead: Lessons, calculators, live market context and daily analysis — each one useful on its own, and considerably better together.
home.exploreLearnBody: Structured courses that start at first principles and build towards a repeatable trading process.
home.exploreToolsBody: Position size, pip value, margin and profit — worked out before the trade rather than after it.
home.exploreNewsBody: What happened, why it mattered and what it changes — written for people who trade, not for headline readers.
home.exploreAnalysisBody: Chart-led breakdowns and trade ideas from the desk, published as the session develops.
home.exploreGlossaryBody: Plain-language definitions for every term you will meet on a chart, cross-linked as you read.
home.exploreMarketsBody: Rates, trading sessions and currency strength, so you know what the market is doing before you open a chart.
home.exploreAboutBody: Who writes this material, how the site is funded, and what we will never do with your attention.

home.highlightsTitle: Built to be understood, not to impress
home.highlightsLead: Six commitments that shape every lesson, article and definition on this site.
home.highlightPlainLanguageBody: Jargon is defined the first time it appears, and linked to the glossary every time after.
home.highlightWorkedExamplesBody: Numbers are shown being calculated, not asserted — so you can reproduce them on your own trade.

home.highlightFreeToReadBody: Every lesson, article and glossary entry is readable without signing up or handing over an email.
home.highlightMultilingualBody: The site is written to be translated, right down to reading direction — not bolted on afterwards.

refusals.unchecked: Tick the reCAPTCHA box below the keys, then save again.

GOOGLE.apiKeyHint: From Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials. Restrict the key to the Cloud Translation API, and to this server's address if your hosting allows it.
GOOGLE.priceHint: Used to estimate spend. Check Google's current price for Cloud Translation Basic.

translate.sealKeyMissingBody: The key is stored encrypted, and the server needs TRANSLATE_SECRET_KEY in its environment to do that. Set it (32 random bytes, base64) and restart.

refusals.keyRequired: Enter an API key for this provider first. A key saved for another provider is never sent to this one.

reasons.not_configured: Automatic translation is off, or no key is saved.
reasons.seal_unavailable: The saved key cannot be opened. Check TRANSLATE_SECRET_KEY on the server, then enter the key again.
reasons.auth_failed: The provider refused the key. Check that it is correct and still active, and for Google that the Cloud Translation API is enabled and its restrictions allow this server.
reasons.quota_exceeded: The provider account's translation quota is used up.
reasons.rate_limited: The provider is limiting requests right now. Try again in a minute.
reasons.budget_exceeded: This month's character budget is reached. Raise it, or wait for next month.
reasons.provider_error: The provider had an error. Try again later.
reasons.network_error: The provider could not be reached.
reasons.internal_error: Something went wrong on our side while translating. The failure is logged; try Sync again, and report it if it repeats.

languages.howBody: Add a language from the list, then fill its interface text under Interface text, by hand or automatically, and write its legal site text under Site text. Then turn on its Live switch: its pages, its entry in the language menu and its sitemap entries appear at once, and content is translated automatically in the background. Turning it off hides it from the public site again and deletes nothing. Any number of languages can be live at the same time.

marketData.title: Market data
marketData.description: The instruments every tool reads, and the provider they come from.
marketData.confirmDeleteBody: Its entire price history is deleted with it and cannot be recovered. Deactivating hides it from every tool and keeps the data.
marketData.emptyBody: Add a currency, pair, metal, index or commodity for the tools to read.
marketData.newDescription: Add something the calculators and the market tools can read.
marketData.editDescription: Change how this instrument is named, quoted and fetched.
marketData.symbolHint: A code like EUR, or a pair like EUR/USD.
marketData.providerSymbolHint: Only when the data provider calls it something else.
marketData.pipSizeHint: Leave empty to derive it from the quote currency.
marketData.providerDescription: Where prices come from, and how often they are refreshed.
marketData.driverHint: Manual keeps the stored history and fetches nothing.
marketData.apiKeySaved: A key is saved — leave blank to keep it
marketData.refreshHint: The shortest gap between calls to the provider. A scheduled sync that arrives sooner does nothing and spends no requests.
marketData.staleHint: Past this, a rate counts as stale. Tools keep printing the date it is from, and the admin surfaces flag it.
marketData.enabledHint: Turning this off stops the nightly sync. Stored prices stay.
marketData.testDescription: Fetches one series through the same path the nightly sync uses.
marketData.secretKeyMissingBody: Without it a saved API key cannot be read back, so saving one here would look like it worked and never fetch anything. Set the environment variable first.
marketData.manualBody: The Manual provider serves whatever price history is already stored. Tools that need rates say so rather than failing.
marketData.syncDescription: Fetches daily bars for every active instrument, oldest first, and stops when the request budget runs out.
marketData.nextDueUnscheduled: Only when a scheduler calls the sync endpoint

toolsAdmin.title: Trading tools
toolsAdmin.description: The eight tools the site offers, and every word and default on them.
toolsAdmin.editorDescription: Everything this tool says, and the defaults it opens with.
toolsAdmin.enabledHint: A tool that is off returns 404 and leaves the tools bar entirely.
toolsAdmin.contentDescription: The title, the one-line tagline, the intro and the explainer below the widget.
toolsAdmin.configDescription: Defaults, limits and which instruments this tool offers. What it computes is fixed in code.
toolsAdmin.relatedDescription: Picked first, then topped up automatically to the count below. An empty list is fine.
toolsAdmin.mediaDescription: Shown behind the title on this tool's page. The plain brand banner is used when this is empty.
toolsAdmin.seoDescription: What search engines and social cards show for this tool.
toolsAdmin.settingsDescription: Whether the tool is live, and how its related strip behaves.
toolsAdmin.taglineHint: One line under the title. Shown on the tools index too.
toolsAdmin.introHint: Two or three sentences above the widget.
toolsAdmin.bodyHint: The longer piece below the widget — formulas, caveats, how to read the result.
toolsAdmin.relatedCountHint: How many to show. Anything not picked above is filled in automatically.
toolsAdmin.faqDescription: Questions answered under this tool, and emitted as FAQPage structured data.
toolsAdmin.faqRemoveBody: It is removed from this tool when you save.

config.rateMarkups: Typical markups over the mid-market rate
config.rateMarkupsHint: Estimates only, attributed to no named provider. They are applied to the stored mid-market rate, which is never changed.
config.componentsHint: Weights are relative and are normalised — they need not add to anything. A component with too little history is left out and counted, never filled in with a zero.
config.riskLevelsHint: Above the moderate limit, a trade is shown as aggressive.
config.minRecommendedRatioHint: Below this ratio, the calculator notes that the reward is small for the risk.

related.emptyBody: The strip fills itself automatically until you pick something here.

highlights.description: Up to six cards, shown in a band under the calculator. Leave it empty and the band does not render.
highlights.emptyBody: Without at least one card the band is absent from the public page rather than empty.
highlights.dialogDescription: One reason a reader should use this tool. Plain text — no links or formatting.
highlights.textHint: Two or three lines. Say what the calculator does, not what a broker charges or pays.
highlights.removeBody: It is removed from the list here. Nothing is written until the tool is saved.

ai.title: AI usage
ai.description: What AI has cost this month, which features spent it, and who used them.
ai.offBody: No AI feature appears anywhere in the admin while the global switch is off. Turn it on under Budget & limits.
ai.noProviderBody: Every feature falls back to the Echo provider, which returns labelled placeholder text and costs nothing.
ai.tileAvailableHint: A call is refused when its worst case would not fit, so the last few dollars go unused.
ai.budgetCappedBody: Every AI feature is hidden until the budget is raised or the month rolls over on the 1st, UTC.
ai.budgetCappedNotifyOnly: AI keeps working: the cap behaviour is set to notify only.
ai.chartEmpty: No AI calls in this period yet.
ai.recentDescription: The log records what a call cost and who made it. It holds no prompt and no output, by design.
ai.featuresDescription: Which features exist is decided in code. What each one may use, and whether it appears at all, is decided here.
ai.featureGlobalOff: The global AI switch is off, so this feature does not appear anywhere yet.
ai.featureMaxTokensHint: Lower than the built-in ceiling of {ceiling}. The effective limit is the smallest of this, the request ceiling, and the model's own.
ai.featureInstructionsHint: House style only — appended to the instruction, never replacing it. {count} of 1000 characters.
ai.featureCostPerCall: About {cost} per call at current prices
ai.featureCostUnknown: Cost unavailable — no provider is enabled

featureDesc.form_fill: Drafts every text field of an editor from a short brief, and rewrites any one field on request. You review before anything is replaced. Long pages need Max output tokens per request raised to about 8000.
featureDesc.writing_assistant: A toolbar menu in every rich-text editor: draft, expand, change tone, summarise, fix grammar.
featureDesc.seo_generation: Fills the SEO section of every editor that has one. You review each field before it is applied.
featureDesc.translation: Fills an empty locale's draft from the source, flagged as machine-translated until a human saves it.
featureDesc.summarization: Writes an excerpt and a key-takeaways list into the editor's own fields.
featureDesc.alt_text: Describes an image for a screen-reader user, into the media library's alt-text field.
featureDesc.quiz_generation: Drafts questions from a published lesson, into the quiz editor. Nothing is saved until you press Save.
featureDesc.writing_studio: A panel on every admin page for text that has no field yet: draft from a topic, rewrite, paraphrase, fix grammar, change the tone, and aim for a character or word count. Results are copied out by hand; nothing is saved.

featureWhere.form_fill: Top of every editor, and the sparkle menu beside each text field
featureWhere.seo_generation: The SEO section of the article, course, lesson, video, glossary and tool editors
featureWhere.writing_studio: The AI Writer button in the admin header (Ctrl/⌘+J)

ai.limitsDescription: The global switch, what AI may spend in a month, and which model each tier resolves to.
ai.limitsEnabledHint: With this off, no AI control appears anywhere in the admin. Every editor is exactly what it was before AI existed.
ai.limitsBudgetHint: 0 means no cap. Changing this rewrites the cap for the CURRENT month, not just future ones.
ai.limitsWarnHint: When the amber banner appears and the first notification is sent.
ai.limitsCapHint: Stopping is the safe default. Notify-only exists because the CMS having to keep working and the spend having to stop can genuinely conflict.
ai.limitsMaxTokensHint: A ceiling over every feature. The effective limit is the smallest of this, the feature's own, and the model's.
ai.limitsRate: Maximum calls per person per hour
ai.limitsRateHint: A stop for a stuck client loop, not an anti-abuse control — everyone here is already staff.
ai.tiersDescription: A cost decision made once, applied everywhere. Changing a tier re-points every feature that falls back to it.
ai.tierLightHint: Mechanical work: alt text, translation, grammar fixes.
ai.tierHeavyHint: Drafting, expanding and tone — where quality is visible in the output.
ai.tierMissing: No enabled model has this ID. Features fall back to the default provider's first model.
ai.resetDescription: Sets the recorded spend for {period} back to zero. The usage log is untouched; this only clears the counter the cap is measured against.
ai.resetConfirmDescription: The cap starts counting again from zero for {period}. The call history stays. This is recorded in the audit log.
ai.providersDescription: Where generation is sent, the key it is sent with, and the models and prices behind each one.
ai.providerEditDescription: The endpoint, the credential and the models. Editing this is editing where every prompt goes.
ai.providerLabelHint: What this provider is called on the features screen.
ai.providerBaseUrlHint: Leave blank for the provider's own endpoint. Only set this for a proxy or a compatible gateway.
ai.providerApiKeySaved: A key is saved. Type a new one to replace it; leaving this blank keeps the stored key.
ai.providerEnabledHint: A disabled provider is never selected, even by a feature that names it.
ai.providerDefaultHint: Where a feature goes when it names no provider of its own. Exactly one provider is the default.
ai.providerDeleteDescription: Its models go with it, and any feature pointing at it falls back to the default provider. The stored key is destroyed.
ai.providerSecretMissingBody: Keys are sealed with it, so a key saved now could never be read back. Add a 32-byte base64 value to .env and restart the dev server — an edited .env does nothing until then, and an absent key looks exactly like a rejected one.
ai.providerEchoBody: Echo needs no key and reaches no network. It returns labelled placeholder text so every screen works before a real provider exists.
ai.modelsDescription: Prices are data, not code: correct one here rather than in a deploy. Every spend figure is dated with the most recent change.
ai.modelEditDescription: The provider's own model ID, and what it is billed at per million tokens.
ai.modelIdHint: Exactly as the provider spells it, for example claude-opus-5.
ai.modelCachedPriceHint: Leave blank to price cache reads as ordinary input, which is the honest answer when the provider does not report them separately.
ai.modelDeleteDescription: Features pointing at it fall back to their tier. Usage already recorded keeps the cost it was charged at.
ai.modelsEmpty: No models yet. Add one before enabling this provider.

reasons.missing_key: The provider has no API key
reasons.secret_unreadable: The stored key cannot be opened — check AI_SECRET_KEY
reasons.content_too_large: The content is too large to send
reasons.model_no_vision: The model this feature uses cannot read images — turn on “Reads images” for it under AI → Providers, or pick a model that can
reasons.provider_timeout: The provider did not answer in time
reasons.invalid_output: The result did not match what was asked for

ai.assistantActionsHint: Works on the text you selected in the editor, or on the whole body if nothing is selected. It keeps the text's own language unless you pick a different one above; grammar fixes never translate. The result appears under the editor for you to insert, replace or discard.
ai.seoDescription: Tick the fields to apply. A field you have already written is left unticked, and nothing is saved until you save.
ai.translateConfirmDescription: The text in this locale is replaced by a machine translation. Nothing is saved until you save the article, so you can still discard it by leaving without saving.
ai.takeawaysDone: Takeaways written — review them before saving
ai.quizDescription: Drafts questions from the lesson this quiz belongs to. Nothing is saved until you save the quiz, and you can edit or reject any of them first.
ai.quizEmpty: No questions came back. Try a smaller number, or a lesson with more prose.
ai.fillDescription: Describe what this page should cover. AI drafts the text fields below; you review before anything is replaced, and nothing is saved until you save.
ai.fillBriefPlaceholder: For example: a beginner lesson on pips and pip value, with a worked EUR/USD example
ai.fillLanguageHint: Follows the Language selector on the Content section
ai.fillReviewDescription: Tick the fields to apply. Empty fields are ticked for you; fields you have already written are not. Nothing is saved until you save.
ai.fillApplied: Draft applied — review it, then save
ai.fillTokenHint: A long draft can be cut off by the output limit. If this keeps happening, raise Max output tokens per request under AI, Budget & limits.
ai.fieldReviewDescription: Replace the field with this suggestion, or discard it. Nothing is saved until you save.

method.statistic: Each cell is a correlation coefficient between −1 and +1. At +1 the two pairs moved in lockstep; at −1 exactly opposite; near 0 their moves were unrelated.
method.returns: We correlate daily returns, not prices. Two pairs both drifting upward look correlated at the price level even when their day-to-day moves have nothing to do with each other.
method.minimum: A cell with less history than the window shows a dash rather than a number. A coefficient worked out from a handful of days is not a small measurement, it is a wrong one.
method.cadence: The figures are updated once a day, from the last completed daily close. The page says when that was.

risk.empty: None of the {total} markets in the basket has enough stored history yet, so there is no score to show. One appears once the platform has a few weeks of daily closes.
risk.historyNote: One point per day the score could be worked out.

method.score: A single score from 0 to 100. Above the upper threshold is risk-on, below the lower one is risk-off, and in between is neutral.
method.rank: Each market is scored by where its latest move sits within its own recent range — its percentile rank. A market that usually moves half a percent and has just moved two ranks near the top of its own history, whatever the absolute number.
method.direction: Markets that rise when risk is being taken on score as they rank. Markets that rise when risk is coming off have their rank flipped before it is counted. The weighted average of what is left is the score.
method.excluded: A market with too little history is left out and counted, never filled in with a zero. A zero would be a claim that the market was flat; leaving it out is the truth, which is that we do not know.
method.cadence: The score is worked out once a day, from the last completed daily close. The page says when that was.
method.notAdvice: It describes what has already happened. It is not a forecast, and it is not a recommendation to do anything.

marketNews.sourcesBody: Every headline belongs to the provider that filed it. Nobody here writes, edits or selects them, and a story appearing here is not a view we hold.
marketNews.scheduleBody: Most of what moves a currency was on a calendar days before it was news. Knowing what is due is worth more than reading about it afterwards.
marketNews.cautionTitle: A headline is not a signal
marketNews.cautionBody: By the time a story is published the market has usually moved. Read it to understand what happened, not to decide what to do next.

liveRates.marketHoursBody: Forex trades around the clock from Sunday 5 PM to Friday 5 PM New York time, passing through the Sydney, Tokyo, London and New York sessions.
liveRates.spreadBody: The gap between the bid and the ask is set by the broker you trade with, so it is not shown here. Spreads are usually tightest while London and New York overlap, and widen around major news and in thin markets.
liveRates.riskBody: Prices can move quickly on economic releases, news and shifts in sentiment. Check a price with your own broker before acting on it, and always manage your risk.

volatility.title: Volatility tracker
volatility.lead: How far each currency pair and commodity has been moving, measured from its daily highs and lows. Use it to judge risk and to set stops that suit the market as it is.
volatility.cardTagline: How far each pair has been moving, session by session.
volatility.emptyBody: None of this group's instruments has any daily bars yet. Figures appear once market data has been collected.
volatility.understandLead: A session's range is its high minus its low, as a percentage of its close. The level reads the current figure against these bands:

levelBodies.medium: Ordinary movement for most major pairs.
levelBodies.high: Wider swings. Give stops more room.
levelBodies.extreme: Very large swings, common around big news and in exotic pairs.

tips.highBody: Trade a smaller size, so a wider stop still risks the same amount.
tips.lowBody: Tighter stops and targets fit, but a breakout can be a false start.
tips.breakoutBody: A range that widens after a quiet stretch often marks the start of a move.
tips.newsBody: Ranges widen around scheduled releases. Check the economic calendar first.

methodology.range: Each session's range is its high minus its low, divided by its close, as a percentage.
methodology.windows: Daily uses the last session, Weekly the average of the last 5 and Monthly the average of the last 22. These are trading sessions, not calendar days.
methodology.average: The average covers the last 66 sessions, about three months. Trend is the current figure minus that average, in percentage points.
methodology.cadence: The figures come from daily bars and change once a day. They describe sessions that have already closed, and they are not a forecast.

openAccount.question: How do I open a trading account?
openAccount.answer: Opening an account is simple. Click 'Sign Up' on our homepage, choose your account type, complete the registration form, verify your identity, and make your first deposit. The entire process typically takes {fromMinutes}-{toMinutes} minutes.

minimumDeposit.question: What is the minimum deposit required?
minimumDeposit.answer: The minimum deposit depends on the payment method you choose. Our deposit and withdrawal requests are typically processed within a minimum of {fromMinutes} minutes and up to a maximum of {toHours} hours. To view your exact deposit limits and available methods, please log in to your client portal. You can start trading with as little as {minimumDeposit}.

withdraw.question: How can I withdraw my funds?
withdraw.answer: You can withdraw funds using the same method you used for your deposit. Withdrawals are processed within a minimum of {fromMinutes} minutes and up to a maximum of {toHours} hours. During weekends and public holidays, processing may take up to {holidayHours} hours. We also offer instant withdrawal services for selected payment methods.

platforms.question: What trading platforms do you offer?
platforms.answer: We are licensed by MetaQuotes and provide you with the industry-leading {platform} trading platform. Our clients can access {platformShort} through the web terminal, mobile apps for iOS and Android, and desktop applications for Windows and Mac. All versions offer advanced charting tools, real-time price feeds, fast execution, and a full suite of professional trading features.

hours.question: What are your trading hours?
hours.answer: The forex market operates {hoursPerDay} hours a day, {daysPerWeek} days a week. Trading opens on Sunday at {opens} and closes on Friday at {closes}. On our platform, market hours are displayed in {platformTimeZone} for your convenience. Additionally, cryptocurrency trading is available {cryptoHours}, allowing you to trade anytime — even on weekends and public holidays.

education.question: Do you offer educational resources?
education.answer: Yes, we provide comprehensive educational materials including trading courses, live webinars, platform tutorials, market analysis, and a complete trading glossary. All resources are free for our clients.

leverage.question: What is leverage and how does it work?
leverage.answer: Leverage allows you to control larger positions with smaller capital. For example, with {leverage} leverage, you can control {position} with just {margin}. While leverage can amplify profits, it also increases risk, so proper risk management is essential.
